title: Airflow, Lift and Drag
src: Practice questions written for Glidepath from the Aviator's Handbook, Part 2, 2-11 to 2-19 (not printed in the book: the Handbook has no question bank)

add.q: At the leading-edge stagnation point:
o: Velocity is zero and static pressure is maximum
Velocity is maximum and pressure minimum
add.ex: Air is brought to rest: total pressure = static pressure, dynamic pressure zero.

add.q: The boundary layer is defined as the layer in which flow speed is less than:
Typical boundary-layer thickness at the leading and trailing edges is about:
Compared with a laminar boundary layer, a turbulent boundary layer:
o: Has more skin friction but resists separation better
Has less skin friction and separates sooner
Has less skin friction and resists separation
add.ex: Its higher kinetic energy lets it face the adverse pressure gradient.

add.q: The transition point moves forward when:
o: The surface is rougher or the speed is higher

add.q: Increasing sweepback (same area) causes:
o: Higher CLmax and higher stalling angle
Higher CLmax and a lower stalling angle
Lower CLmax and a higher stalling angle
add.ex: Swept wings behave like low-aspect-ratio wings.
